description: F-CORE-042 with the OTHER predicate, on the shipped pack: `de-kleinunternehmer` is the first module in the library that says NO by forbidding rather than by requiring. § 19 Abs. 1 UStG raises no tax on a small business's turnover, so an entry that books 4040 (Erlöse Kleinunternehmer) together with an output-VAT account shows tax on a supply that owes none — and § 14c Abs. 2 UStG then makes it owed anyway, which is the expensive half: the books are wrong AND the money is due. WHY THIS RULE IS SAFE AND THE IG-LIEFERUNG RULE WOULD NOT BE, because that is the reasoning a later pack author needs and it is not obvious: `forbidAccountIn` refuses a COMBINATION inside one entry, so it is only usable where the combination cannot occur legitimately. A collective invoice may perfectly well carry a taxable and an intra-community supply at once, which is why 4030 gets no such rule — it would refuse a correct entry. 4040 cannot be in that position: the § 19 status holds for a whole calendar year (§ 19 Abs. 1), so no single document mixes small-business and standard-rate turnover. WHAT THE RULE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SAY is the input side. § 19 Abs. 1 Satz 4 UStG denies the input-tax deduction too, but an input-tax posting carries no revenue line, so a rule hung on 4040 would never fire — that prohibition depends on the tenant's PROFILE and the constraint vocabulary has no conditional. Naming the gap here is better than a rule that looks like it covers it. The last step is the edge: § 13b and the intra-community acquisition stay owed by a small business (§ 19 Abs. 1 Satz 3), those entries touch 3100 without any revenue account, and they must go through untouched.

expect.comment: Balanced, vouchered, in an open period, every account known — and legally impossible. Without the rule this posts and the VAT return then declares 19.00 of tax the business is not entitled to collect but, having shown it, owes under § 14c Abs. 2.
The same money, booked the way § 19 requires: gross is net, nothing is split off. The rule forbids a line; it does not move an amount.

The § 17 module and this one meet here without colliding: a reduction of a tax-free supply is booked against the revenue account it reduces, so it never reaches 4020 and never needs a correction. Two constraint modules add up; neither replaces the other.

input.text: Leistung eines EU-Unternehmers, § 13b — der Kleinunternehmer schuldet die Steuer trotzdem

expect.comment: The edge that proves the rule is narrow enough. § 19 Abs. 1 Satz 3 keeps § 13b alive for a small business, so 3100 legitimately carries a balance — and this entry has no revenue line, so the prohibition never triggers. A rule that had been hung on `tax_out` in general instead of on 4040 would have refused this.
